governanceNotes: Deferral reason (2026-09-23, D1 batch 26): the DSM-5 merged dyspareunia and vaginismus into genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder because the Lahaie 2015 experimental study found large overlap between the conditions despite statistical fear/muscle-tension differences - a dyspareunia -> vaginismus edge would assert a direction DSM-5 declined to draw, and the conditions share the same identity space. Genital pain did not differ between the groups.

Outgoing evidence barrier: the dyspareunia-to-depression/anxiety literature is descriptive-only (Carlson 2026 StatPearls; Fernandez-Perez 2023 review background) without cohort denominators, and the Yong 2017 deep-dyspareunia cohort measures depression symptoms as correlates of tender-site exam findings in an endometriosis referral population - below the repo's authoring bar (diplopia precedent). Revisit only if a qualified human accepts descriptive evidence or a dyspareunia-specific outcome cohort appears.
